messages.subject: i levels
parts:
Further to my graph question, 

I created categorical variables with my thresholds being

light 45.8
mod 93.2
vigorous 418.3 

code used:
     #User defined activity levels, 
     ilevels=c(0,45.8,93.2,418.3,8000),
     iglevels=TRUE,

However this created overlapping variables
inactive: 0-45.8
light : 45.8-93.2
mod 93.2-418.3
vig 418.3 +

I don't know if it makes a difference in the grand scheme of things, however would adding more levels address the issue for eg:

#User defined activity levels, 
     ilevels=c(0,45.7, 45.8,93.1,93.2,418.2,418.3,8000),
     iglevels=TRUE,

this would I think generate the following variables, including the ones in bold 
Which means that I would have to drop the variables in bold. 
What is your advice?

Variables output:

inactive 0-45.7

45.7-45.8 

light:45.8-93.1 

93.1-93.2

mod: 93.2-418.2

418.2-418.3

vig: 418.3-8000

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] i levels
parts:
Hi Martinique,

The ranges in your first attempt do not overlap. GGIR always uses [start, end) windows, meaning including start excluding end. This is documented in 
https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRoutput.html at "[A,B)_mg_0-24h_ENMO"

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
